meta.notes: Initial profiling based on technical documentation, GitHub repository, and demo experiments

technical_architecture.model_type: Single-stage language model with audio tokenization
technical_architecture.codebook_structure: 4 parallel codebooks with flattening pattern strategy
technical_architecture.parameter_count: Small: 300M params, Medium: 1.5B params, Large: 3.3B params

architecture_details.encoder: EnCodec - convolutional encoder-decoder with residual vector quantization
architecture_details.conditioning: Text embeddings via T5 encoder or audio continuation

interface_characteristics.interaction_paradigm: Batch generation - specify parameters upfront, wait for output
interface_characteristics.learning_curve: Moderate - requires Python environment setup and CLI comfort

hardware_requirements.minimum_gpu: NVIDIA GPU with 16GB+ VRAM (for large model)
hardware_requirements.cpu_only_mode: Possible but extremely slow (not practical for creative workflow)

composition.notes: Generates novel musical content from text descriptions

arrangement.notes: Can continue existing melodies, but arrangement control is limited

sound_design.notes: Strong timbral generation, particularly for electronic textures

performance.notes: No real-time interaction - batch processing only

mixing_mastering.notes: Outputs raw generated audio without mixing/mastering capabilities

temperature.impact: Controls randomness - higher = more variation, lower = more deterministic

top_k.impact: Restricts sampling to top-k most likely tokens - lower = less diversity

top_p.impact: Nucleus sampling threshold - alternative to top-k

cfg_coef.impact: Classifier-free guidance strength - higher = stronger prompt adherence

model_size.impact: Larger models: better quality, slower generation, more VRAM

usability.rationale: CLI-based interface accessible to technical users, but lacks GUI for broader accessibility. Python setup required.

generation_speed.rationale: Large model: ~2-3 minutes for 30s generation on RTX 4090. Not suitable for rapid iteration.

audio_quality.rationale: Produces coherent audio but with noticeable EnCodec artifacts (metallic timbre, compression). Strong for electronic, weaker for acoustic.
audio_quality.evidence_source: Generated demo outputs, technical paper (Copet et al. 2024)

semantic_alignment.rationale: Demo shows reasonable interpretation of text prompts for rhythm/genre, but specificity (e.g., 'funky bassline') is unpredictable.

steerability.rationale: Multiple control parameters (temp, top-k, cfg_coef), but relationship between parameter tweaks and musical outcomes unclear.

workflow_impact.rationale: Batch processing paradigm requires generate-then-evaluate cycle. No real-time feedback during creative flow.

daw_integration.rationale: No plugin format. Outputs must be manually imported to DAW. No tempo/key metadata embedded in files.

creative_adaptability.rationale: Text prompts enable exploration, but lack of fine-grained control may frustrate specific creative intentions.

known_limitations: EnCodec artifacts: Metallic/compressed timbre even in high-quality outputs
No tempo parameter: Cannot specify BPM, only describe via text ('upbeat', 'slow')
No key/scale parameter: Harmonic control limited to text descriptions
Monophonic bias: Struggles with dense polyphonic textures
Duration ceiling: 30-45s practical limit, longer generations risk coherence loss
No structural control: Cannot specify verse/chorus/bridge sections explicitly
GPU dependency: Impractical for users without high-end hardware
Non-deterministic: Same prompt + parameters can yield different results
known_strengths: Open source: Full code and model weights available for research/modification
State-of-the-art architecture: Single-stage generation avoids cascaded error accumulation
Strong electronic textures: Particularly effective for synth-based genres
Melody conditioning: Can continue existing musical ideas (audio-to-audio mode)
Active development: Regular updates and bug fixes from Meta AI team
Comprehensive documentation: Technical paper + GitHub README + tutorials
Multiple model sizes: Tradeoff between quality and resource requirements

evidence_sources.citation: Copet, J., Kreuk, F., Gat, I., Remez, T., Kant, D., Synnaeve, G., Adi, Y., & Défossez, A. (2024). Simple and Controllable Music Generation. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 36.
evidence_sources.relevance: Technical architecture, training methodology, baseline comparisons

evidence_sources.relevance: Installation instructions, API documentation, parameter specifications

evidence_sources.citation: Meta AI. (2024). MusicGen Demo. Hugging Face Spaces.
evidence_sources.relevance: Hands-on preliminary experiments, output quality assessment

evidence_sources.citation: Meta AI Blog. (2023, June 12). Introducing MusicGen: Text-to-music generation.
evidence_sources.relevance: Use case examples, design motivations, comparison to prior systems

next_steps.phase_1_focus: Conduct 7-9 creative sessions generating funk track elements (basslines, drums, synth leads) to assess real-world workflow integration
hypotheses_to_test: EnCodec artifacts will be more pronounced in acoustic instruments than electronic textures
Semantic alignment varies by musical domain (rhythm vs. harmony vs. timbre)
Prompt specificity inversely correlated with output predictability
Post-processing (EQ, compression) will be necessary for all outputs
next_steps.documentation_strategy: 152-widget session log for each session, capturing prompts, parameters, outputs, technical observations, emotional state, and reflexive synthesis

reflexive_notes.evaluator_positionality: As an electronic music practitioner, I may be more tolerant of EnCodec artifacts in synthetic textures but critical of acoustic instrument generation. My background in computer science may also make CLI interaction easier than for non-technical musicians.
reflexive_notes.methodological_concerns: Preliminary assessment based on 45 minutes of exploration may not capture subtle capabilities/limitations revealed through extended creative use. Phase 1 sessions essential to validate/challenge these initial scores.
questions_raised: Will generate-then-curate workflow become natural or remain disruptive?
Can parameter tweaking compensate for semantic alignment gaps?
How much post-processing is 'acceptable' before system becomes a 'sample generator' rather than 'composition assistant'?
